captions.instagram:
Myth: a donation only helps your taxes if you itemize.
Fact: starting with tax year 2026, you can deduct cash gifts to qualified charities without itemizing.

✔️ Up to $1,000, or $2,000 if you file jointly.
✔️ Cash means cash, check, card or bank transfer to a qualified organization. Check it with the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search.
✔️ Gifts to individuals, including a friend's fundraiser page, are not deductible.
✔️ Keep a bank record or a written receipt from the charity.

Giving Tuesday is December 1. Gifts made by December 31 count for 2026.

Source: IRS Topic 506, Charitable contributions. General information, not advice for your situation.

captions.youtube_description: Starting with tax year 2026, people who take the standard deduction can deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 joint) of cash contributions to qualified charities. Gifts to individuals are not deductible, and noncash gifts don't qualify for this one. Keep a bank record or receipt. Giving Tuesday is December 1; gifts by December 31 count for 2026. Source: IRS Topic 506.
